These people thought they worked for Apple. The store was fake.
Kunming, July twenty eleven. An American blogger walks into what looks like a real Apple Store.
The glowing sign, the wooden tables, the winding staircase, staff in matching T-shirts.
But the paint job is sloppy, and the name tags just say: staff.
The blogger asks around. The staff truly believe they work for Apple.
Down the road there's another one. Its sign says: Apple Stoer.
Back then, Apple had just four real stores in China. None in Kunming.
The photos go viral. Officials inspect about three hundred shops.
Weeks later, they count twenty-two unauthorised Apple stores in Kunming alone.
Two get shut down. Not for copying Apple. For not having business licences.
And the iPhones? Local reports said several of those stores sold genuine Apple products.
The only fake thing was the store.
In China, the real thing is out there. Find it at laowai dot ma.
